description: Green Infrastructure is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by EPA, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. When rain or snow hits the ground, it can pick up trash, chemicals, and other pollutants as it flows into storm drains and out into local streams, rivers, and lakes. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Rainfall-induced, Water Quality. Assets: Aquatic and Marine Resources, Cultural and Community Services, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – Stormwater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
